extracted.intended_audience: general public; NPR listeners/readers interested in business, utilities, and California wildfire/regulatory news
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting on a utility company's planned Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in response to potential wildfire liabilities, covering legal, financial, regulatory, and operational implications. Focuses on the PG&E case (wildfire investigations, liability estimates, management changes, asset-sale options, and court/regulatory actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: California utility liability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: California law says utility companies can be held liable for fire damage caused by their equipment, even if they weren't negligent in maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cal Fire determined PG&E equipment had sparked 17 wildfires across Northern California in 2017; in 12 of those fires the agency's findings were referred to county District Attorney's offices for potential violations of state law. This liability standard can expose utilities to very large claims even absent traditional negligence findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC filing liability estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: If PG&E is found legally responsible for some or all of the costs connected to the 2017 and 2018 Northern California wildfires, its liability could exceed $30 billion, according to the company's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That figure does not include potential punitive damages, fines and penalties or damages related to future claims. The filing also notes awareness of about 50 complaints on behalf of at least 2,000 plaintiffs for the Camp Fire and approximately 700 complaints on behalf of at least 3,600 plaintiffs related to 2017 fires, some seeking class-action status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bankruptcy notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The company is required by law to give 15 days' notice of bankruptcy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electric and natural gas customers will not notice any change in service, the utility said. The 15-day notice is a procedural requirement before a Chapter 11 filing becomes effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 11 as a court-supervised resolution mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: "We believe a court-supervised process under Chapter 11 will best enable PG&E to resolve its potential liabilities in an orderly, fair and expeditious fashion," interim CEO John Simon said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 11 can enable a company to access capital and resources to continue operations while restructuring liabilities. It is presented as a mechanism to resolve mass claims in an orderly way, but legislative or political intervention could alter outcomes; past reorganizations have had significant consequences for ratepayers and investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from headline liability figures (punitive damages/fines/future claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported liability estimates may exclude punitive damages, fines and penalties, and damages from future claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing company exposure, consider both the SEC-disclosed estimate (e.g., $30 billion) and the potential for additional categories of loss that are not included in that number; these exclusions can materially increase ultimate costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset sales to fund wildfire claims
rubrics_metrics.description: PG&E has been exploring selling off its natural gas unit and other assets; 'All net proceeds from the sale of PG&E's gas division would be used to set up a fund to pay billions of dollars in potential claims from wildfires.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company is also exploring selling key real estate assets, including its San Francisco headquarters; proceeds from such sales are being positioned as a way to raise funds specifically earmarked to pay claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management change as regulator appeasement
rubrics_metrics.description: PG&E's decision to replace its chief executive is likely intended to satisfy state regulators rather than investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making management changes is characterized as something the state is looking for and may placate regulators; such changes are often public gestures aimed at restoring regulatory/official confidence during investigations or enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-proposed operational safety measures (grid inspection, vegetation management, power shutoffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A federal judge proposed requiring PG&E to re-inspect its entire electric grid and 'remove or trim all trees that could fall onto its power lines.' During the 2019 wildfire season, the company would also be required to turn off power in parts of the grid if windy conditions make them unsafe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court-ordered remedial measures can include large-scale inspections, vegetation management, and preemptive power shutoffs; these operational requirements can affect service reliability, customer experience, and the company's costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle that customers should not pay for utility negligence
rubrics_metrics.description: "The debt that PG&E is talking about is debt that arises directly from its own negligence and liability... it's a longstanding principle of utility law that customers don't pay for that kind of thing," said Mindy Spatt of The Utility Reform Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer advocates assert that ratepayers should be protected from costs stemming from a utility's negligence; this principle factors into debates about restructuring, bailouts, and how claims should be allocated between shareholders, bondholders, and customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation and prosecutor referral process
rubrics_metrics.description: Cal Fire determined PG&E equipment had sparked multiple wildfires and referred findings to county District Attorney's offices for potential violations of state law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or agency investigations (e.g., Cal Fire) can trigger criminal or civil referrals to prosecutors, which may lead to separate legal exposures beyond private civil claims and can influence bankruptcy strategy and public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical bankruptcy precedent and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: This would be the company's second bankruptcy filing in two decades; the utility's 2001 reorganization following widespread blackouts led to a negotiated rate increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past reorganizations can set expectations for outcomes (e.g., rate increases, negotiated settlements) and inform debates about who bears costs (ratepayers vs. investors) and the political feasibility of legislative protection for the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market and credit rating impacts as indicators of financial distress
rubrics_metrics.description: Shares of PG&E Corp. had plummeted more than 51 percent as of 3 p.m. ET; the company has lost more than two-thirds of its market value since the Camp Fire, and Moody's downgraded its credit rating nearly to junk status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharp share-price declines and credit-rating downgrades signal market recognition of elevated liability risk and can constrain financing options, making restructuring or asset sales more likely.
